paper.title: A Self-Evolving Agentic Framework for Metasurface Inverse Design
paper.central_claim: Coupling a fixed coding agent, a fixed differentiable solver (TorchRDIT) and a deterministic physics evaluator with a meta-agent that revises a human-readable SKILL.md from solver-grounded per-task feedback raises held-out same-type task success from 38% to 74% (CPF 0.51->0.87, attempts 4.10->2.30) and the evolved skill also transfers to new-type families (92%->90% and 20%->90%).

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; configured type haiku -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] per dispatcher

Figures 2, 3, S5.1 are images; values taken from captions and prose only

evidence.quote: skill evolution raises same-type task success from 38% to 74%, the fraction of physical criteria met from 0.51 to 0.87, and reduces average attempts from 4.10 to 2.30
evidence.support_explanation: Headline same-type test-split result (author-reported).

evidence.quote: Rather than updating model weights, it revises the skill files from solver-grounded feedback, while the base model and differentiable solver, which provides the physics simulation and gradients, stay fixed.
evidence.support_explanation: States evolved object (skill files) and what is held fixed.

evidence.quote: The rule is elitist: the incumbent best is replaced only by a strictly higher-ranked candidate, so a revision that ranks no better on validation is never deployed.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention/acceptance rule for skill files (validation SG with fixed tie-break order).

evidence.quote: Every split uses fixed 50/15/50 train/validation/test partitions.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection (15 val) vs report (50 test) split sizes.

evidence.quote: Because each template is assigned to a single split, no task is used for both training and testing
evidence.support_explanation: Template-level split; test templates unseen in training.

evidence.quote: on Same-type, 18 of the 31 baseline failures are rescued (58%) with zero regressions, and on New-type-B, 35 of 40 are rescued (88%) with zero regressions.
evidence.support_explanation: Paired rescued/regressed counts against the starter-skill baseline.

evidence.quote: New-type-A, already near ceiling, rescues one of its four baseline failures but regresses two previously passing tasks, for a net change of one task (92% to 90%), so its success rate is not strictly monotone.
evidence.support_explanation: Reports a non-improving transfer setting and regressions.

evidence.quote: this is within-class learning from validation rather than transfer to an unseen class
evidence.support_explanation: Authors scope the New-type-B gain as within-class acquisition because the validation family shares the test device class.

evidence.quote: validation success rises from 53% at the seed skill to 100% at iteration 1. No later candidate surpasses it
evidence.support_explanation: Same-type final skill is the iteration-1 rewrite; later iterations never replace it.

evidence.quote: the median cost per task falls from $3.24 to $0.42 on Same-type (about 87%) and from $3.73 to $0.76 on New-type-B (about 80%)
evidence.support_explanation: Per-task LLM spend for starter vs evolved skill; evolution (training) cost not given here.

evidence.quote: The present evidence remains bounded by one solver stack, one benchmark design, and one base model
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' own scope limit.

evidence.quote: Even so, these systems can complete a task-specific workflow but do not retain solver-specific tactics in a form that later tasks can reuse
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap statement against LLM+solver inverse-design systems incl. their own MCP framework.

evidence.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first study to examine the evolution of skills in agentic metasurface inverse-design workflows.
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty claim is domain-specific.

evidence.quote: A separate deterministic evaluator scores each candidate with physical simulation rather than model self-assessment
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier is external and deterministic.

evidence.quote: First, the evolved skill file is much more operational: it moves beyond a starter API guide and spells out how to read prior context, parse training results, group task types, and update reusable guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative description of what changed in the retained artifact (92-line starter vs 218-line evolved).

evidence.quote: In this work, both the meta-agent and the coding agent use Claude Sonnet 4.6, and skill evolution is performed for four iterations.
evidence.support_explanation: Single model, four iterations, no seeds mentioned.

evidence.quote: each template generates individual tasks that differ only in their numerical targets
evidence.support_explanation: Within-template tasks are near-duplicates; effective sample size smaller than 50.

evidence.quote: Further details of the generic skill-evolution procedure, including the skill-combination step that merges features from multiple candidate skill files, are given in the original work
evidence.support_explanation: Meta-agent revision procedure is deferred to prior work (MCE, ref 21), not specified here.

evidence.quote: We deliberately use parameterized design families with attainable optima rather than open-ended free-form topology optimization
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark built so optima are attainable; controlled but narrow.

evidence.quote: yet reaches only 13% on the 15-task validation family that drives the loop
evidence.support_explanation: New-type-A: validation rises while test is flat; validation signal not predictive of test change.

evidence.quote: These reference documents are generated by the environment and are not themselves rewritten by the meta-agent during skill evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Only SKILL.md is evolved; static reference subtree is fixed.

gap.author_gap: LLM-coding-agent systems for inverse design (incl. authors' MCP framework) finish a task-specific workflow but do not retain solver-specific tactics for later tasks.
gap.checked_gap: Specific, concrete in-domain limitation (no cross-task reuse of solver tactics); it is a limitation of the authors' own and two other cited systems, which are not locally pinned.
gap.lineage: Ancestor/nearest neighbor for the mechanism is meta context engineering (ref 21, bi-level skill/context revision) and prompt/memory-updating agents (refs 22-25); this paper instantiates MCE on metasurface design with a physics evaluator. Versions of refs 21-25 not available locally.
gap.closest_adjacent: Generic skill/memory evolution agents already solve cross-task reuse of textual guidance; the paper does not state what they leave unsolved for solver-grounded science tasks beyond domain novelty.
gap.residue: Retention of solver-specific tactics across tasks; paper gives no frontier comparison to other skill-evolution methods.
gap.stakes: Repeated per-task attempts and cost (median $3.24 per same-type task for the starter skill).
gap.method_response: Evolve SKILL.md from evaluator-grounded records, select on validation, reuse on later tasks.
gap.remaining_gap: Only one solver/model/benchmark; no evidence that iterative evolution (vs one rewrite) or the feedback signal drives gains; cross-class transfer not established.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbor skill-evolution papers (refs 21-25) not available locally in the pinned inputs; closest-adjacent comparison cannot be checked here; requested in batch notes.

claims.text: Skill evolution improves same-type held-out task success and efficiency.
claims.setting: Claude Sonnet 4.6 coding+meta agent, TorchRDIT, 50 test tasks from held-out sibling templates of G2-G6
claims.selection_vs_test: selected on 15 validation tasks; reported on separate 50 test tasks
claims.result: SG 38%->74%, CPF 0.51->0.87, attempts 4.10->2.30; 18/31 failures rescued, 0 regressions
claims.denominator: N=50 single run; tasks within template differ only in numeric targets
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this benchmark the iteration-1 evolved skill outperforms the starter skill on unseen sibling templates; effect of iteration count and feedback is not isolated.

claims.text: The evolved skill transfers to new-type families.
claims.setting: New-type-A (train G1-3, val G4, test G5/G6/Gaux) and New-type-B (reverse)
claims.selection_vs_test: validation family G4 shared by both; same class as New-type-B test families
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within-class convention acquisition from validation is shown (B); cross-class transfer is not established (A is flat, near ceiling), as the authors themselves state.

claims.denominator: per-task medians; training cost not included
claims.allowed_conclusion: Inference-time cost reduction at fixed task set; total cost including evolution unknown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A single rewrite of a 218-line SKILL.md (selected on 15 validation tasks) raises author-reported held-out success from 38% to 74% on sibling templates and, in the within-class New-type-B setting, from 20% to 90%, without regressions in those two settings, on one solver, one model and one benchmark.
unresolved: Whether the gain is due to evolution procedure/feedback vs richer static documentation (no human-written or no-feedback control)
Whether iterations beyond the first matter

G.reason: A real, concrete limitation (no reuse of solver-specific tactics across tasks) is stated against three in-domain systems, but nearest generic skill/memory-evolution methods (refs 21-25) are not compared on what they fail to solve, and the stated novelty is domain-first.

M.reason: Bi-level loop with external physics feedback is a coherent response to the gap, but the revision procedure is deferred to prior work, and no distinguishing prediction vs a richer static prompt or a human-written skill is offered.

X.reason: Skill file schema, per-batch revision, validation selection with a fixed tie-break order, elitist replacement, archival and the fixed (non-evolving) reference subtree are all specified; meta-agent prompt/revision content, conflict/expiry handling and the skill-combination step are not.

E.measurement.reason: Deterministic physics-solver criteria with binary SG plus CPF/BM are a credible verifier outside the LLM; criteria are derived from published designs with attainable optima. The benchmark is author-constructed and templated, so thresholds' difficulty calibration is untested.

E.causality.reason: Single controlled swap of the retained artifact (starter vs evolved skill, same model/solver/test set) isolates that skill content matters, with paired rescued/regressed counts; but no alternative improver, feedback-off, human-written-skill or equal-compute control, and the same-type gain comes from one rewrite (iteration 1).

E.holdout.reason: Template-level train/val/test partitions with a separate 50-task test split and two role-swapped family-heldout settings; authors disclose that New-type-B validation shares the test class. Near-duplicate tasks within templates and no pretraining-contamination audit keep it below 4.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes, execution-failure rates and regression counts are reported, including a negative setting, but there is a single run per setting, no confidence intervals, no seeds, and no variance of the evolution trajectory.

E.cost.reason: Per-task dollar cost and attempt counts for starter vs evolved are reported with matched model and retry caps, but the one-time evolution cost (meta-agent revisions, training and validation runs) is not reported in the main text or appendices read.

rationale: Skill-file evolution在物理求解器反馈下确实提升了留出同类模板成功率(38→74%)，评估器可信、划分较清楚；但是无替代改进器/无反馈对照，增益来自一次重写，缺方差与总演化成本，跨类迁移未建立。
